title: CELIAN catalog entry
description: One abstract brick and, for each target, the concrete service that implements it. One file per brick: catalog/<id>.yaml. Rules the schema cannot express (dates against today, file name, links to ADR and BENCH files, SPDX list) belong to the catalog check. Decision: docs/adr/ADR-009-catalogue.md.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema that the entry follows.

id.description: Abstract brick name, also the file name without .yaml.

summary.description: What the brick provides, in one line.

declared_by.description: spec: the project spec declares the brick. target: the brick follows from the target and the spec never names it.

targets.description: Every MVP target is required (ENF-02). A target outside the MVP is added by a new schema version once Lucas opens it.

line80.description: Single line of text, no leading or trailing blank.

line200.description: Single line of text, no leading or trailing blank.

line300.description: Single line of text, no leading or trailing blank.

text500.description: Free text, possibly on several lines.

date.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD, written as a quoted YAML string. The catalog check rejects impossible dates and dates in the future.

version.description: Exact version, never a range or a tag such as latest.

spdxExpression.description: SPDX license expression without parentheses. The catalog check matches each identifier against scripts/catalog/accepted-licenses.yaml, the license allowlist written by CELIAN.

status.description: Upstream status. The schema accepts the three values so that a change can be written down; the catalog check fails on anything but active (principle VI).

model.description: foundation: carried by a foundation. community: community organisation without a foundation. single-vendor: one company.

body.description: Name of the foundation, organisation or company.

detail.description: Where the project sits in that body, in one line.

standards.description: Open standards or protocols the service exposes. They hold principle II. An empty list means the target layer carries the whole difference. A new value is added here, with its source in catalog/README.md.

url.description: Official source: project repository or site, foundation page, provider documentation.

establishes.description: The facts this source establishes for the entry.

adr.description: ADR that put this service in the catalog.

bench.description: Benchmark behind the ADR. A managed service imposed by principle III may have none.

artifact.description: Digest of a downloaded binary, recorded in CELIAN so that a later substitution upstream is caught.

pendingItem.description: A field still open. A target with pending items is a valid catalog entry that no blueprint may use yet (principle IV).

ossTarget.description: Free and open source component, run by the generated project.

last_release_on.description: Date of the latest upstream release. The catalog check fails 12 months after it (principle VI).

verified_on.description: Date of the latest full verification. Equals the most recent read_on of the sources.

managed_gap.description: Cloud targets only: why no managed service of the provider covers the need (principle III).

managedTarget.description: Managed service of the cloud provider. No license field: the service is proprietary and runs under the provider terms.

version.description: Engine version when the provider offers several, such as a database major version.

verified_on.description: Date of the latest full verification. Equals the most recent read_on of the sources.

localTarget.description: PC target: free and open source only (principle III).

gcpTarget.description: GCP target: the provider managed service, or an open source component with the reason no managed service covers the need (principle III).
